title: Autosurgeon: admin shelllets and deterministic runbook playback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, auditable set of 'shelllets' (small, parameterized admin primitives) plus a deterministic runbook playback engine that lets support engineers execute complex remediation flows safely and reproducibly. The goal is to replace ad-hoc runbook copy/paste with composable primitives that enforce safety checks, require explicit approvals for dangerous steps, and produce machine-readable provenance for post-incident review.
acceptance_criteria: A set of 12 core shelllets implemented (inspect, drain-node, rollback-deploy, invalidate-cache, annotate-tenant, escalate-to-oncall)
Playbacks run in staging reproduce exact sequence and state transitions recorded in a runbook log
Safety guardrail triggers for 3 classes of dangerous ops (mass user impacts, data-destructive, cross-region) with mandatory two-person approval
Console UI surface shows per-step status, who approved, runtime telemetry and tokenized cost estimate
Audit log exported to S3 and visible in the unified incident timeline dashboard
implementation_notes: Shelllets are implemented as idempotent task definitions with typed inputs and output contracts (JSON schema)
Use existing operator-sidecar pattern for privileged execution; reuse ENG-531210 operator-sidecar auth surface where possible
Playback engine stores deterministic event stream (timestamp, step-id, inputs, actor, approval-hash) to ensure replayability
Integrate KMS signing for approval receipts; minimal UX flow to request/confirm approval via Slack interop
Design to allow future synthetic dry-run mode (no external side effects) for training and QA
rollout_plan: MVP alpha in internal staging with dev-oncall only (2 weeks)
Collect safety telemetry and tune guardrail thresholds (1 week)
Beta roll to support team with training session and a curated set of shelllets (2 weeks)
Gradual availability in prod for non-destructive shelllets; gated release for destructive operations behind security review
Post-launch retrospective and a plan to migrate 10 high-frequency ad-hoc scripts into shelllets
test_plan: Unit tests for shelllet input validation and idempotency
Integration tests that run playback against a sandbox cluster with recorded golden fixtures
Chaos test: simulate partial step failure and validate automatic compensating actions or safe aborts
Manual QA checklist for approval flow, Slack modal integrity, and audit export correctness
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive actions. Mitigation: two-person approvals, KMS-signed receipts, and mandatory dry-run for first 5 uses per shelllet
Risk: privilege escalation via operator-sidecar. Mitigation: least-privilege tokens, ephemeral creds, and periodic access review
Risk: replay drift if external systems change. Mitigation: record environment hashes and require confirmations when drift detected
Risk: support team adoption. Mitigation: create curated playbooks for common incidents and run hands-on training sessions
